questiontext.text:
Write down the first four terms of an arithmetic sequence whose fourth term is {@kk@} times the first term.

First Term = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Second Term = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

Third Term = [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

Fourth Term = [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

truefeedback.text:
Worked solution:

An arithmetic sequence takes the form \(a,\, a+d,\, a+2d,\, a+3d, \dots\) where \(a\) is the first term and \(d\) is the common difference. The \(n\)th term of the sequence can be obtained by substituting the first term and common difference in the general formula \(a_n=a+(n-1)d\).

In this case, the fourth term in the sequence should be {@kk@} times the first term, that is \(a_4= {@kk@}a\).

If we use the formula for the \(n\)th term to write \(a_4= a+3d\), we obtain the equation \( a+3d={@kk@}a\). Solving the equation for \(a\) we get

\( a+3d= {@kk@} a \)

\({@kk@}a-a=3d\)

\( {@(kk-1)*a@}=3d\)

\( {@work_sol_last@}\)

This equation has infinitely many solutions and any solution would lead to a correct answer. For example, we can choose \(d={@d_mod_ans@}\), so that \(a={@a_mod_ans@}\).

The first 4 terms of the sequence will then be

\( a = {@a_mod_ans@} \)

\( a_2 = {@a_mod_ans@}+{@d_mod_ans@}= {@a_mod_ans_2@} \)

\( a_3 = {@a_mod_ans@}+2 \times {@d_mod_ans@}= {@a_mod_ans_3@} \)

\( a_4 = {@a_mod_ans@}+3 \times {@d_mod_ans@}= {@a_mod_ans_4@}. \)
